$comment: Single configuration source for the NodeMation pipeline. Workflows contain mechanics only; every name, label, policy and target lives here. A loader workflow syncs this file into Redis key cfg:pipeline; every workflow reads that key at the start of a run.

labels.$comment: hold = not approved; pr_open = a PR exists; shipped = merged; needs_triage = a person must look; spec_present = the issue already carries its scenarios, so triage is skipped and the spec marker is set directly.

ingress.$comment: Every event the stages consume, subscribed on every repository hook by deploy/ensure-repo-hooks.sh. Events are the path; the poller is the full backup.

merge.$comment: A human-approved PR merges when GitHub reports one of accept_states; for any state other than clean every counted check (ci.checks) must also have a conclusion in ok_conclusions, so a red non-required job cannot hold an approved PR.

dependabot.author: dependabot[bot]
dependabot.$comment: Dependency-bot PRs are pre-approved. Tested means: every required status context on the base branch is green; if the branch declares none, every check run named in `checks` is green. Other jobs never block.

chain.$comment: Ordering inside a stream. Primary: GitHub issue dependencies (blocked_by). Fallback when that API is unavailable: a body line '<blocked_by_line> #N'.

build.$comment: Build stage: the build-queue consumer dispatches this workflow on the runner; the job runs the coding agent in a fresh checkout and opens the PR as the bot. max_turns and timeout_minutes bound one run; an unfinished build is a failed build: its commits stay on the branch, no PR is opened, the ticket gets the reason, and restoration continues from the branch. claim_minutes is how long an approved issue with no PR stays claimed before the sorter releases it again; max_attempts caps those releases, after which the hold label comes back. Issues in skip_repos are never released to the build queue (their tickets are worked by the operator, not the runner).

feedback.$comment: A submitted review that requests changes on a pipeline PR becomes a feedback build on the same branch (code review only; questions belong on the ticket). Dedupe per review id.

ci.$comment: Which check runs count as the tests of a pull request when the base branch declares no required status contexts.

repair.$comment: A failing required (or configured CI) check on a pipeline PR becomes a repair build on that PR's branch. Attempts are counted per PR; at the cap the PR and its issue get a comment and the needs-triage label and nothing more runs.

branch_protection.$comment: Applied to every active repository's default branch by deploy/ensure-branch-protection.sh. The check context is required only where the repository produces it (a workflow job named like the context); requiring a context a repo never reports would block it forever. require_up_to_date=false: a branch that is merely behind its base still merges; with dismiss_stale_reviews on, forcing an update commit would dismiss the approval it was waiting on. reviews_override: repositories the pipeline owns need a pull request but no approval, so its own repair PRs can merge without a person (Brian, 2026-09-21).

pipeline_repair.$comment: A failed run of the build workflow becomes a pipeline-repair item: the agent reads the run, fixes the cause in the dispatch repository (PR, labelled, auto-merged when auto_merge is true), or comments on the ticket that caused it, or files a ticket in operator_repo for the operator. One claim per run id, max_per_day repair runs, never for a run that was itself a repair.
pipeline_repair.label: pipeline-repair
